text: A system of systems is formed when separately useful systems interact to deliver a capability beyond their individual contributions. Members may remain under different management and be located far apart. The arrangement can change over time and show effects that cannot be assigned to a single member. Distance and evolution are often present, but neither is a universal requirement.

items: Illustration: A sensing service, a coordination centre and a response organization each perform their own work. Together they can support a coordinated detection-and-response outcome.

text: Check for independent member purposes and a distinct outcome created by cooperation.
Several components under one manager are not automatically a system of systems.
